hostContracts.kind: process-global MainActor environment replacing Monaco standalone singleton services
members: initialize(overrides) exactly once before the first service access or editor/model/provider registration
registerLinkOpener and registerCodeEditorOpener retain Monaco last-registered-first traversal and return disposables
hostContracts.freezeRule: first service access freezes overrides; later initialize calls return alreadyInitialized and change nothing; test processes isolate environment state by process
hostContracts.fallback: no opener handles external resources; nil command returns unhandled; nil workspace host retains the core open-model-only workspace capability; nil logger drops logs

members: applyExternalOperation(operation,index,transactionID) async -> operation result and optional undo receipt
hostContracts.rule: open Mona model mutations are never delegated to the host
a host may advertise transactional or textOnlyTransactional only when prepare makes commit allocation-free with no externally reportable failure

hostContracts.routing: component command registry executes first; only an unhandled provider or LSP command reaches the host; result installation revalidates session and request identity

hostContracts.rule: logging cannot reenter editor APIs, block the MainActor, contain document text or change control flow

members: state: connecting, open or closed with typed reason
hostContracts.rule: transport never parses frames or JSON; L2-R2/R3 codec owns every byte above this boundary
the component never searches PATH, launches a process, opens a socket or downloads a server; a macOS Process adapter exists only in the sample host

hostContracts.itemIdentity: unique stable item ID plus original model, modified model, label, description and immutable host metadata
hostContracts.rule: duplicate IDs reject the whole new snapshot; retained IDs preserve collapse, active and scroll state

defaultWithoutHost.domain: all target URIs must resolve to currently open Mona models; an unresolved URI fails before any mutation

failureHandling.abort: apply documentChanges in protocol order; stop at first failure; earlier successful operations remain applied and failedChange identifies the failing index
failureHandling.transactional: preflight every open-model change and host external operation, await host preparation, revalidate every DependencyStamp, call the prepared host's nonthrowing commit, swap all prepared model roots, enqueue the complete event batch, then drain
failureHandling.textOnlyTransactional: when the edit contains only text document changes, use the transactional path; when any create, rename or delete exists, use abort semantics for the entire ordered edit
failureHandling.undo: apply in protocol order; on failure attempt receipts and open-model inverse elements in reverse order; applied=false is returned even when every undo succeeds because the protocol gives no rollback guarantee

workspaceEditStateMachine.changesMapOrder: for the unordered WorkspaceEdit.changes map, sort URI keys by raw UTF-16 lexicographic order before assigning failedChange indexes
workspaceEditStateMachine.advertisement: client capabilities equal the selected host capability exactly and never claim a stronger failure handling or resource operation set
workspaceEditStateMachine.atomicCommitInvariant: no await, allocation, host callback or fallible operation occurs between prepared host commit and prepared model root swaps
workspaceEditStateMachine.eventInvariant: transactional paths enqueue the entire model event batch before drain; abort and undo paths emit each committed or inverse model event in actual operation order

callbackAndThreadingRules: Live model and editor APIs remain MainActor synchronous.
An async host callback receives immutable Sendable request data and never receives a mutable model root.
Every async result returns through the owning MainActor session, version and request gate.
No host callback occurs inside PreparedModelCommit root swap or GlobalModelEventHub queue mutation.
Cancellation, disposal or LSP session replacement invalidates outstanding callback generations.
A callback contract violation becomes a typed host failure and never silently upgrades advertised capabilities.
